what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for a dimensional variation to maintain the grandfathered status of the 53 Oak Avenue lot; one member abstained.
Members agreed informally that the merger doctrine does not apply, because one of the two adjoining lots is conforming.
The board debated whether a variation was needed at all, then granted it as added protection against a court challenge.
The permit is contingent on compliance with all applicable regulations; the decision goes to the town clerk, followed by a 20-day appeal period.
Assessor records and an abatement were discussed, including an assessing error that had made the lot one acre and buildable.

why_it_matters: The ruling decides whether the Oak Avenue lot stays a separate buildable lot, which affects what can be built there and how it is assessed for property tax.
The 20-day appeal window means the decision is not final until it passes, so a neighbor or other party could still challenge it in that time.
watch_next: Filing of the decision with the town clerk, and the end of the 20-day appeal period that follows.

meetings.headline: Zoning board granted a special permit for a garage-and-apartment addition at 36 Summer Street with a reduced side setback.
meetings.summary: The board heard Peter M Kelly's application to add two garage bays with an apartment above at 36 Summer Street, in the Summer Street overlay district. Members questioned the commercial use, the five-foot side yard against the fifteen-foot standard, rental plans, egress and fire access. A motion to grant the permit with prior conditions and Board of Health requirements was made and seconded, and the permit was announced as granted. The board then adjourned.
